In summary, our research is concerned with
the occurrence of nitrosamines at the different steps of the water treatment, and in samples of a chlorinated STP effluent.

the occurrence of nitrosamines, especially NDMA and N- nitrosodiethylamine, in the different steps (raw water, treated and highly treated water, and ozonated and chlorinated water) of a DWTP, and in chlorination and ozonated samples from a STP effluent and a reservoir.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of nitrosamines at concentrations higher than those reported in other studies was detected in chlorinated samples, especially after ozonation and highly chlorination processes.

the nitrosamines are not a significant problem for drinking water quality, although the presence of NDEA at high levels in the STP and the presence of NDMA and N-DEA above the guide value in the DWTP should be highlighted.
NDMA and N-nitroso-dimethylethylamine (NDEME) are the most important compounds in terms of concentration, followed by NDEA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nitrosamines are formed in the chlorination process of STP effluents, and the concentrations are high enough to cause health problems.
nitrosamines are not present at concentrations above the MDLs in the raw and treated water of DWTP.
nitrosamines can be detected at low concentrations in water samples, and the combination of automated SPE with isotope dilution-GC/HRMS is an excellent method for their analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method based on automated SPE and isope dilution GC/ HRMS is suitable for the determination of nitrosamines, with low MDLs and high precision, in water samples.
the automated SPE and isope dilution GC/MS method is a suitable technique for the analysis of NDMA in water samples.
automated SPE coupled with GC/HRMS is a very useful and efficient method for the analysis of trace concentrations of nitrosamine compounds in water.
